plan_a_advantages: More targeted hill work (hill repeats and long runs) for trail-specific strength.
Includes longer runs to build a robust aerobic base.
Incorporates active recovery days for better recovery and injury prevention.
plan_b_advantages: More concise and shorter workouts, potentially appealing to runners with limited time.
Includes cross-training for varied stimulus and reduced impact.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted hill work and longer runs, crucial elements for trail-specific speed development. While Plan B includes some hill sessions, it lacks the consistent volume of hill-focused training and the longer runs that build the aerobic base necessary for sustained trail efforts. Plan A’s emphasis on moderate-paced long runs and dedicated hill repeats directly addresses the demands of trail running, whereas Plan B’s focus on threshold work feels somewhat isolated and less reflective of the varied terrain and sustained effort required on trails. Furthermore, the inclusion of active recovery days in Plan A is beneficial for preventing overtraining and promoting recovery, which is vital for consistent progress.
